title: Login and checkout failures
executive_summary: Login and checkout 5xx errors began at 09:29-09:30Z, roughly one minute after auth-service was deployed (2.13.4 to 2.14.0 at 09:28Z). Auth-service logs show repeated 'unsupported key type EC in JWKS' errors under the new jose-4.2 validator. Error rates rose on auth (~0.3% to ~27%), api-gateway (~0.5% to ~19%) and payment-service (~0.8% to ~14%), in the order the dependency graph predicts. Latency and DB saturation are unchanged, consistent with fast validation rejections. Most likely cause: the auth-service 2.14.0 JWT validation migration. Rollback is recommended; it has not yet been verified.

hypotheses.description: auth-service 2.14.0 deployment (JWT validation migrated to jose-4.2) rejects EC keys in JWKS, causing token validation failures for login and downstream checkout. Mechanism: After deploy dep-cbc63772 at 09:28, auth-service raises TokenValidationException 'unsupported key type EC in JWKS (validator=jose-4.2)'. Token validation fails, auth returns 5xx, api-gateway (which validates/forwards auth) and payment-service (dependent on auth) surface 5xx; users are logged out when sessions cannot be validated.

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): deployment_regression in auth-service - auth-service 2.14.0 deployment (JWT validation migrated to jose-4.2) rejects EC keys in JWKS, causing token validation failures for login and downstream checkout.
corrective_actions: Roll back auth-service to 2.13.4 (dep-cbc63772 reverse) immediately and verify auth/gateway/payment error rates return to baseline
Hold the jose-4.2 migration until EC key support in the JWKS validator is fixed and tested
preventive_actions: Add a pre-production canary test that validates tokens signed with every key type published in JWKS
Gate auth-service deploys on automated post-deploy error-rate checks with auto-rollback
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on auth-service TokenValidationException count and error rate >2% for 5 minutes
Track api-gateway and payment-service 5xx rate split by upstream auth dependency
limitations: Historical incident search was not run
Telemetry is limited to the investigation window and baseline; no post-rollback data exists yet

Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The evidence points to the auth-service 2.14.0 deployment as the probable root cause. Its JWT validation fails on EC keys, and the failures spread to api-gateway and payment-service. Confidence is not yet ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED because the rollback has not been tested, the JWKS contents were not inspected, and downstream logs were not pulled.
